summary.root_cause_text: Config change by ops set queue_max 1000 -> 0, so every enqueue was rejected as 'queue full' and orders were silently dropped.
recommended: Have customers or the upstream resubmit the dropped orders (ids 17-35 and any later ones), since the in-memory queue lost them.
Add validation that rejects queue_max=0, and add an alert on the dropped counter.

events.text:
version: v1.3
payment_provider_url: internal://payments-v1
queue_max: 0
worker_count: 1
sync_interval_s: 5
queue_max: 0 -> 1000. Confirmed: the service is now using the new value.
All business invariants green (health, payments, queue, worker, ledger, errors, latency).
The dropped orders are not recoverable with my tools, because they were never persisted to the queue.

root_causes: Config change by ops set queue_max 1000 -> 0, so every enqueue was rejected as 'queue full' and orders were silently dropped.
evidence: recent_changes: config: queue_max 1000 -> 0 (worker tuning) by ops

args.impact: 19 orders dropped before processing (as of last reading), never paid. money_impact queued_orders: count 19, SAR 3284.05, USD 1445.98, total_sar 8706.48. Dropped orders were not recovered.
recommended_actions: Have customers or the upstream resubmit the dropped orders (ids 17-35 and any later ones), since the in-memory queue lost them.
Add validation that rejects queue_max=0, and add an alert on the dropped counter.
args.summary: A config change set queue_max to 0, which made the queue drop every new order silently while /health stayed green. I restored queue_max to 1000 and check_invariants is now green. The orders dropped during the window were lost and need to be resubmitted.
